text:
Predicates:
CanRegister(x) ::: x can register to vote in the United States.
Participate(x) ::: x can participate in the 2024 United States presidential election.
CitizenshipUS(x) ::: x has United States citizenship.
CitizenshipTWN(x) ::: x has Taiwanese citizenship.
Official(x) ::: x is a Russian Federation official.
Manager(x) ::: x is a manager at Gazprom.
HoldTWN(x) ::: x holds Taiwanese citizenship.
Vladimir ::: Vladimir.
Ekaterina ::: Ekaterina.
Premises:
∀x (CanRegister(x) → Participate(x)) ::: Everyone who can register to vote can participate in the election.
∀x (CitizenshipUS(x) → CanRegister(x)) ::: If someone has US citizenship, then they can register to vote.
∀x (CitizenshipUS(x) ∨ CitizenshipTWN(x)) ::: A person either has US or Taiwanese citizenship.
¬∃x (Official(x) ∧ HoldTWN(x)) ::: No Russian Federation official holds Taiwanese citizenship.
¬HoldTWN(Vladimir) ∧ ¬Manager(Vladimir) ::: Vladimir neither holds Taiwanese citizenship nor is he a manager at Gazprom.
CanRegister(Ekaterina) ∨ Official(Ekaterina) ::: Ekaterina can register to vote, or she is a Russian Federation official.
Conclusion:
¬Official(Vladimir) ::: Vladimir is not a Russian Federation official.
